prompt: Create a high-fidelity desktop web application UI design comp for APIShield, a local Python API migration and AI repair tool. This is a designed application screen, flat front-facing screenshot, landscape 16:10, not a poster, not an angled device mockup. Exact product truth: synthetic shipping project, a POST endpoint moved from /labels to /labels/create; consuming function create_label in src/parcel.py; declared business rule Preserve package identity and exact integer grams; linked pytest test test_shipping_preserves_package_and_weight. One AI-generated repair passed one configured test and one linked business-rule test. Original code unchanged. Display compact badge 'Design concept' somewhere unobtrusive. Graph shows these existing relations only, not invented transitive dependencies or analytics. Beautiful professionally art-directed components, strong alignment, purposeful clear grouping, carefully placed buttons, precise icons, high-quality type, readable labels. Main navigation simple: Workspace, Runs, Settings; Help visible as a small affordance. Project selector 'Shipping API'. Persistent short sequence Check changes → Explore impact → Review repair. Always one clear primary action, 'Review repair'. Existing recorded report, not actively running, no fake percentage or inflated metrics. Code shows before /labels and after /labels/create, payload unchanged. Include a short contextual help sentence rather than paragraphs. Tight professional component proportions and deliberate visual hierarchy, no generic icon-card grid, no huge marketing headline, no gradients/glow, no decorative illustration, no graphs unrelated to the task. This is static design imagery; do not label animation as already implemented. Direction B: DEVELOPER WORKBENCH. An exceptionally polished modern dark IDE-style application with charcoal #161b24, graphite panes #222a36, readable off-white #f1f4f8, subtle steel dividers and soft cornflower blue #82a8fa for interactive selection. No neon, no luminous borders. Typography a crisp workhorse sans with 24px title, 14px controls, professional mono for file paths/diff. Composition is genuinely a developer workbench: 60px icon rail with tooltips visually represented, top project breadcrumb and compact Help, then a 160px contextual change navigator listing one endpoint change and related file. Central largest pane is a readable dependency graph with 4–5 substantial, finely crafted node components: API change, consuming function, business rule, linked test, new endpoint. Sparse lines distinguish source observation versus declaration. Right 34% pane is a source editor with actual green/red diff lines and file tabs. Bottom full content width is a short evidence drawer with tabs Tests / Business rule and concise Passed rows. The main action Review repair is top-right and visually obvious; secondary Download patch restrained beside code. Stable balanced spatial hierarchy, exact baseline alignment, excellent visual comfort, hover/selected affordances, resizable dividers and compact tab highlights. Add an inline 'New here? Follow the shipping example' hint that can be dismissed, not a blocking onboarding modal. Panels flat and nuanced, purposeful depth, cohesive custom components. Should look like a premium engineering product people enjoy using for hours.
note: Visual proposal only. Generated code, dates, avatars and evidence labels must be replaced with actual backend truth; no authentication or invented business-rule proof.
